title: ElTo World
description: One ElTo world: a complete theme package from bootloader to mouse cursor, with real character (wallpaper sets, sounds, dock variants, notch modes). Extends the shell theme.json format (version 1/2). schema_version 3 is the versioned contract: worlds without schema_version are treated as schema 2. Every layer section is optional; a missing layer stays at its default, and the shell must ignore values it does not implement.

name.description: World slug, matches the directory name under elto-worlds/worlds/.

id.description: Stable world id. Required at schema_version 3; should equal name. Used for the installed package, the sound theme and bundle identity.

label.description: Human name shown in the Themes page.

version.description: 2 = world format (kept for the v1/v2 tooling). The versioned contract is schema_version.

schema_version.description: 3 = versioned world schema: id, defaults, asset lists, sounds, compatibility. Absent means schema 2.

license.description: License of the world definition itself.

assetsLicense.description: Fallback license of bundled art; per-asset licenses live in the assets manifest.

identity.description: World character: a one-line story and a signature detail that makes the world distinct.

compatible.description: Versions this world expects. Free-form level strings; the tool warns instead of failing on a mismatch.

defaults.description: World defaults applied on apply/reset. User overrides live in ~/.config/elto/theme.json and win until 'elto-world reset' restores these.

wallpaper.description: Default wallpaper from the world's set.

dock.description: Dock variant: 'island' (implemented), 'bar' (next), more later. Unknown values fall back to island.

notchMode.description: Known values: show (default), hidden, auto-hide (collapsed strip that reveals on hover after a short delay). Unknown values warn visibly and fall back to show, per the approved review; they are not hard errors.

notchRespectFullscreen.description: Stay hidden while a window is fullscreen.

sounds.description: World sounds on by default. User can disable; never forced.

assets.description: Asset manifest. sha256/bytes are required inside .elworld bundles, optional while the world lives in git (assets pending).

kind.description: wallpaper, sound, greeter, boot, cursor, icon, preview, other.

shape.description: Geometry and material tokens. The Trail data contract (per Trail coordination, pending user review) adds the file/presentation tokens below; the vocabulary of values is Trail's contract with the shell and file manager, and a reader must ignore values it does not implement and fall back, never fail.

glass.description: Translucency amount, 0 opaque to 1 fully glass; meadow sits at 0.4.

folderArt.description: Folder icon artwork style, e.g. meadow's "luna".

cardArt.description: Card/panel artwork treatment, e.g. meadow's "gloss-band". Band worlds derive their band colors from the world palette (colors/roles), never hardcoded band colors.

folderView.description: Default folder view in the file manager, e.g. meadow's "details".

options.description: Shell options. Unchanged v1 keys plus wallpapers (the world's wallpaper set).

wallpapers.description: The world's wallpaper set as {path, label} objects, paths under assets/wallpapers/. options.wallpaper stays the active pick for the v1 shell. Plain-string entries fall back to {path: entry} with a warning.

sounds.description: Freedesktop-style sound theme: short wav files per event, played in-process by the shell (no process spawned per event), always disableable.

events.description: Event -> wav asset. Known events: session-start, session-end, notification, drawer-open, drawer-close, lock, unlock, error, wallpaper-change.

layout.description: World behavior and arrangement, not recolor. Declarative: the shell ignores values it does not know and falls back to its default layout.

colorRef.description: A palette token from colors, a role name from roles (resolved role -> token -> hex), or a literal #hex value.

asset.description: Path relative to the world directory, always under assets/.
